findings.claim: The skills' evals were rewritten for the MCP flow but not rerun, so the plan's checked-by item "the skills' evals rerun through skill-creator" and the ticket's done-when (Claude Code's kmaudit-claims-extractor stores claims through the MCP tools with no shell) have no run behind them; the integration test proves install only.
Both results.md files say the tests/test_skills.py checks cover "the agents' tools"; those tools are asserted in packages/kmaudit/tests/test_apm_package.py, not test_skills.py.

verdict.text: The move is done as the plan says.
kmaudit's package holds the two skills and declares the kmaudit server from its own tag.
The Claude-only sub-package holds the two renamed agents with Read, Grep, Glob and their MCP tools, and no Bash or hook.
kmctl's package, wheel and translations no longer carry them.
`set --package kmaudit` pins the server ref and the sub-package version, and refuses when either is missing.
Docs, okf pages and the ADR amendment agree with the code.
Nothing blocks.
The one real gap is f1: no run shows the agents working through MCP.
An operator should run the evals in a session with the kmaudit server before this ships to users.
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` rerun in the worktree, result quoted in Notes.

r1: test_apm_package.py checks the skill set, the `./claude` dependency, `targets == ["claude"]`, the exact uvx args at `kmaudit-v{base_version}`, the exact tools list per agent, and no `hooks` or Bash.
It also checks the five tools exist on the server.
Breaking any of these fails a test.

r2: kmctl tests assert the agents folder holds only kmctl-auditor, the skills list drops the two, the wheel has no kmaudit skill or agent file, and the plugin patch writes only bundle-weaver, event-analyzer and kmctl-auditor for both harnesses.
The auditor and the audit skill stay asserted.

r3: test_release.py covers set moving the server ref (0.1.0 to 0.2.0 to 0.3.0), the line-level diff of the manifest, and the refusals for a missing server and a missing or versionless claude apm.yml, with nothing written.
The `_KMAUDIT_INSTALL` regex does not match the `{git: ...}` comment in apm.yml, so only the server line moves.
r4: I ran the integration test myself: 1 passed.
It installs from a file:// rewrite of a tagged copy and checks .mcp.json, opencode.json, byte-equal agents in .claude/agents/, none in .opencode/agents/, and the skills for both harnesses.

r5: test_skills.py checks no `kmaudit <group>` command in code spans (the group list matches every top-level CLI command), every named `claims_*`/`checks_*` tool exists on the server, the no-agent step, and that agents submit to the namespace folder with `by` set to their name.
The "evals pass" half of the row has no command (f1).
Read the skills and agents against mcp_server.py: `folder`, `answers`, `by`, `brief` and the `concepts`/`path`/`sections`/`claims` fields they name exist.
release.yml stages the claude apm.yml.
kmctl's opencode.py "three agents" docstring is now correct.

The kmctl briefing no longer listing /extract-claims and /write-checks is right: those skills are no longer kmctl's, the harness lists installed skills itself, and kmaudit's own briefing still points at them.
Remaining `kmctl-claims-extractor` mentions are in ADR prose (kept on purpose), log history, prototypes and negative test assertions.
f1 (missing, not blocking): the evals were not rerun.
The reason given holds (the loop refuses a nested claude session), and the plan's spike already showed a subagent can call a project MCP tool.
But nothing shows these agents and skills working end to end.
The fix is to run the evals, not to change code, so I do not need to see it again.
The operator should run it before release.
f2 (docs, not blocking): results.md credits test_skills.py with the agents' tools check.
Name test_apm_package.py for it.
`loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree: lint, format, tests and integration pass; eval rows r1 to r5 pass; "stamp green: 2be1566cbfc5da5665f2042e5657945765ce41255f15bb1b38da20ad79dc716a".
